children: Gulf real-estate markets are expected to remain stable in the second half, despite softer momentum from geopolitical uncertainty, higher construction costs and tighter financing conditions, Kuwait Financial Centre says. Office and industrial and logistics assets should outperform, supported by limited quality supply, infrastructure investment and structural demand. Riyadh prime office rents rose 5.5% on year, with Grade A occupancy around 98%, while Dammam industrial rents increased 9.9%. In the U.A.E., a more measured growth phase is emerging, though Abu Dhabi industrial rents rose 18.2% and office occupancy reached 98%. Kuwait remained comparatively stable despite weaker investment activity.(farhan.rafid@wsj.com)
